mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for three consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month periods of >1% monthly INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL < 1.5% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) over a three-month window signals synchronized demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Positive correlation between GDPC1 and HOUST > 0.7 over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 and HOUST show strong positive co-movement in early-cycle periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a statistical artifact that can occur during population shifts; however, if PAYEMS increases while UNRATE rises due to broader labor force participation, it signals expansion of the labor force without job creation, which typically precedes weaker earnings growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases in the same month
regime_hint: broadening labor force without job creation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which raises corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of >0.5% INDPRO growth.
